This is a C++ project with a greet() function declared in src/greeter.h.

Your task:
1. Find the declaration of greet() using ast-tool:
     ast-tool find src/greeter.h greet
2. Find all call sites of greet() using ast-tool references with the line number from step 1:
     ast-tool references src/greeter.h <line>
3. In src/main.cpp, add the line
     std::cout << "Calling greet" << std::endl;
   immediately before EACH call to greet().
4. Ensure #include <iostream> is present at the top of src/main.cpp.

When done, the file src/main.cpp should compile and contain the logging statement
before every greet() call.

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. NAME
    find - Find AST nodes by type, text, position, or ID.

SYNOPSIS
    ast-tool find [--type <type>] [--grammar <grammar>] [--text <text>]
                  [--id <hex>] [--line <n>] [--column <n>] <file>

DESCRIPTION
    Parse <file> and print every AST node that matches all supplied
    filters simultaneously.  When no filter is given, all nodes are
    printed.

    --line and --column must be supplied together to filter by position.

ARGUMENTS
    <file>    Path to the source file to search.

OPTIONS
    --type <type>       Match nodes whose type equals <type>
                        (e.g. function_definition, identifier).
    --grammar <grammar> Match nodes whose grammar type equals <grammar>.
    --text <text>       Match nodes whose source text equals <text>.
    --id <hex>          Match the node with the given hash. Accepts
                        uppercase or lowercase hex, with or without
                        a leading 0x prefix (e.g. 9E52E360, 0x9e52e360).
    --line <n>          Match nodes that start on line <n> (1-based).
    --column <n>        Match nodes that start at column <n> (1-based).

OUTPUT
    One line per matching AST node:

        <ID> <type> @<line>:<col>[ "<text>"]

    <ID>      32-bit node hash in uppercase hexadecimal.
    <type>    Node type string.
    <line>    1-based source line.
    <col>     1-based source column.
    <text>    Source text of the node, present when non-empty.

EXAMPLES
    Find all function definitions in a file:

        ast-tool find --type function_definition src/parser.cpp

    Find the node at a specific cursor position:

        ast-tool find --line 42 --column 17 src/parser.cpp

    Find all uses of a specific identifier:

        ast-tool find --type identifier --text initialize src/main.cpp

    Look up a specific node by ID:

        ast-tool find --id <node-id> src/main.cpp
---
ast-tool — Source code inspection and semantic analysis.

Inspect AST structure, extract semantic symbols, and trace cross-file
symbol relationships (references, callers, callees) across a workspace.

Usage:
    ast-tool <command> [options]

Options:
    -h, --help    Show this help message.

Commands:

  AST Inspection
    outline     Show the structural outline of a source file.
    find        Find AST nodes by type, text, position, or ID.
    range       Show AST nodes within a source range.
    parent      Show the parent AST node.
    children    Show the child AST nodes.

  Semantic Analysis
    symbols     List symbols in a source file.
    search      Search symbols in the workspace.
    references  Find references to a symbol.
    callers     Find direct callers of a function.
    callees     Find direct callees of a function.

  Cache Management
    cache       Manage the workspace AST cache (warm / status).
    setup       Configure coding-agent session-start hooks.

Run:

    ast-tool help <command>
    ast-tool <command> --help

for detailed documentation of a command.

NAME
    references - Find references to a symbol.

SYNOPSIS
    ast-tool references [--json [--pretty]] <symbol> <root>

DESCRIPTION
    Analyze the workspace rooted at <root>, resolve the named symbol, and
    print every location in the workspace where that symbol is referenced.

    Resolution is semantic, not textual: identifiers are resolved via the
    workspace symbol table, so only genuine uses of the target declaration
    are reported.  Textual grep matches are not included.

    If <symbol> contains '::' it is matched against fully-qualified names;
    otherwise it is matched against unqualified names.  If the query matches
    more than one declaration the command fails with a list of candidates;
    supply a fully-qualified name to disambiguate.

    The declaration site is excluded from results by default.

ARGUMENTS
    <symbol>  Symbol name or fully-qualified name to look up.
    <root>    Workspace root directory to scan recursively.

OPTIONS
    --json      Output results as a JSON array.
    --pretty    Pretty-print the JSON output. Implies --json.

OUTPUT
    Default (plain text), one reference per line:

        <file>:<line>:<col>

    <file>    Path of the file containing the reference.
    <line>    1-based source line of the reference.
    <col>     1-based source column of the reference.

    JSON fields per reference:

        file            Path of the file containing the reference.
        line            1-based source line of the reference.
        column          1-based source column of the reference.
        owning_scope    Lexical scope kind that encloses the reference.

    Output is sorted by file, then by line, then by column.

EXAMPLES
    Find all references to a function named 'parse':

        ast-tool references parse src/

    Find references to a fully-qualified name to disambiguate:

        ast-tool references ast::parse src/

    Export results as JSON for programmatic consumption:

        ast-tool references --json --pretty foo src/
---
NAME
    symbols - List symbols in a source file.

SYNOPSIS
    ast-tool symbols [--json [--pretty]] <file>

DESCRIPTION
    Parse <file> and extract every named semantic symbol, including
    functions, methods, classes, structs, enums, variables, and
    namespaces.

    Each symbol is annotated with its kind, fully-qualified name,
    access modifier, storage qualifiers, and a stable node ID.

ARGUMENTS
    <file>    Path to the source file to analyze.

OPTIONS
    --json      Output results as a JSON object.
    --pretty    Pretty-print the JSON output. Implies --json.

OUTPUT
    Default (plain text), one symbol per line:

        <fqn> <ID>

    <fqn>    Fully-qualified name of the symbol.
    <ID>     32-bit node hash in uppercase hexadecimal.

    JSON fields per symbol:

        kind            Symbol kind (function, class, variable, ...).
        name            Unqualified symbol name.
        qualified_name  Fully-qualified symbol name.
        access          Access specifier (public, protected, private, unknown).
        static          true if the symbol is declared static.
        constexpr       true if the symbol is declared constexpr.
        inline          true if the symbol is declared inline.
        id              32-bit node hash in uppercase hexadecimal.

EXAMPLES
    List all symbols in a source file:

        ast-tool symbols src/main.cpp

    List symbols from a header file:

        ast-tool symbols include/parser.hpp

    Export symbols as JSON for programmatic consumption:

        ast-tool symbols --json src/lexer.cpp

    Export symbols as readable JSON for inspection:

        ast-tool symbols --json --pretty src/main.cpp

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Validation script: checks that a logging statement was added before greet() calls."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

main_cpp = Path("src/main.cpp").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

if "Calling greet" in main_cpp:
    print("PASS: 'Calling greet' found in src/main.cpp")
    sys.exit(0)
else:
    print("FAIL: 'Calling greet' not found in src/main.cpp")
    sys.exit(1)

NAME
    search - Search symbols in the workspace.

SYNOPSIS
    ast-tool search [--name <name>] [--fqn <fqn>] [--kind <kind>]
                    [--file <path>] [--name-regex <re>] [--fqn-regex <re>]
                    [--file-regex <re>] [--json [--pretty]] <root>

DESCRIPTION
    Scan every source file under <root>, extract semantic symbols, and
    print those that match all supplied filters.  When no filter is
    given, all symbols in the workspace are printed.

    Exact filters and regex filters for the same field are mutually
    exclusive (e.g. --name and --name-regex cannot be combined).

ARGUMENTS
    <root>    Workspace root directory to scan recursively.

OPTIONS
  Exact filters (substring match):
    --name <name>       Match symbols whose unqualified name contains <name>.
    --fqn <fqn>         Match symbols whose fully-qualified name contains
                        <fqn>.
    --kind <kind>       Match symbols of the given kind (function, method,
                        class, struct, enum, variable, ...).
    --file <path>       Match symbols in files whose path contains <path>.

  Regex filters (RE2 syntax):
    --name-regex <re>   Match symbols whose unqualified name matches <re>.
    --fqn-regex  <re>   Match symbols whose fully-qualified name matches
                        <re>.
    --file-regex <re>   Match symbols in files whose path matches <re>.

  Output format:
    --json              Output results as a JSON array.
